892.supersedes: The block of 29 Oct 2026 kept the verdict partly_read without seeing any cipher and said 'no decipherment'. New evidence (23 Nov 2026): all five items and the clear draft 8-2-10 fol. 74 were seen at reading size; every ciphered passage has a decipherment or clear text on record (16th-century interlinear decipherments in Malvezzi's originals 8-2-22 and 8-3-10, 19th-century decipherments filed with 8-3-12 and 9-1-2, the clear draft of 8-2-24); HathiTrust full-text search finds deciphered wording of all five in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552; the upstream malvezzi1548 key, unchanged, reads 8-3-12, 8-2-24 and 9-1-2 above their pass marks. Verdict changed to read.

seen.extent: 8-2-22 (Malvezzi to Ferdinand, Constantinople, 24 Mar 1550, Italian; original with four cipher passages of about 46 lines, each line deciphered between the lines; a duplicate in cipher without gloss; 8 images); 8-2-24 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Vienna, 25 Mar 1550, Latin, 26 cipher lines, 2 images; clear draft 8-2-10 fol. 74); 8-3-10 (Malvezzi to Ferdinand, Constantinople, 22 Apr 1550, Italian, about 50 cipher lines, each deciphered between the lines, 2 images); 8-3-12 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Brno, 28 Apr 1550, Latin, original 42 cipher lines and duplicate 29 lines, plus a 19th-century decipherment, 6 images); 9-1-2 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Augsburg, 3 Oct 1550, Latin, 3 cipher lines, plus a 19th-century decipherment, 3 images).
seen.cipher: Graphic-sign homophonic cipher of Malvezzi's alphabet (signs such as circle on a stem, hash, two bars, Greek letters, numerals for doubled letters, null words Cum, Porro, Spo, Dar; code words Ras, ki, ka, zus, zos). Decipherments on or with the leaves: 16th-century Italian glosses over every cipher line of the originals of 8-2-22 and 8-3-10; 19th-century 'Entzifferung' sheets with 8-3-12 (images 5-6) and 9-1-2 (image 3); a modern pencil gloss over lines 1-3 of 8-2-24. Cipher of 8-3-12, 8-2-24, 9-1-2, 8-3-10 fol. 160r and two passages of 8-2-22 transcribed twice (the second blind) and decoded with the upstream malvezzi1548 key (lead892_test/, lead892_rest/).

prior_art.edition: Austro-Turcica 1541-1552, ed. Karl Nehring (Munich 1995), HathiTrust mdp.39015038445451, search only. The archive cites it for 8-2-22 pp. 415-418, 8-2-24 pp. 418-419, 8-3-10 pp. 433-434, 8-3-12 p. 437, 9-1-2 p. 513. HathiTrust full-text phrase searches (23 Nov 2026) taken from the decipherments return this volume for all five items: 8-3-12 'quemadmodum a Rege suo sibi iussum', 'Transmittimus ad te cum hisce', 'mentem dilectionis'; 9-1-2 'de successibus omnibus certiores facere pergas'; 8-3-10 'ogniuno se lamenta', 'aspettano corrieri'; 8-2-22 'nove de Soria', 'non se dechiara el tempo', 'movimento alchuno'; 8-2-24 'pro toto regno nobis permittendo', 'petitionem Transsylvaniae'. So the edition prints the deciphered wording of the cipher passages. Page numbers of the hits could not be displayed.

Neither uses any of these five items. No open issue or pull request names lead 892, Malvezzi or Türkei (gh search, 23 Nov 2026).

892.key_check: Upstream targets/malvezzi1548/KEY_BRIEF.md, unchanged, decoded mechanically from blind transcriptions, against the witness on record, with pass marks in hashed plans and 200 shuffled-key controls: 8-3-12 0.924 of letters (pass mark 0.85; controls best 0.430); 8-2-24 0.875 against its clear draft (0.85; best control 0.428); 9-1-2 0.911 (0.85; best control 0.478); Malvezzi's Italian 8-3-10 fol. 160r 0.783 and two passages of 8-2-22 0.739 against the interlinear glosses (pass mark 0.80 missed; best controls 0.433 and 0.392). The cipher did not change between 1548 and 1550; Malvezzi's own hand needs its own sign links.

892.closed: Read at the time and printed: the ciphered passages of Malvezzi's 8-2-22 and 8-3-10 are deciphered between the lines of the originals in a 16th-century hand; 8-3-12 and 9-1-2 have 19th-century decipherments filed with them; 8-2-24 has its clear draft at Türkei I 8-2-10 fol. 74. HathiTrust full-text search finds deciphered wording of all five in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (pp. 415-418, 418-419, 433-434, 437, 513 as cited by the archive). The upstream malvezzi1548 key reads the Latin letters 8-3-12, 8-2-24 and 9-1-2 unchanged (lead892_test/, lead892_rest/).
